findings.title: Recommendation vocabulary contradicts the arch and the slice's own integration contract
findings.description: The arch (§Gate insertion point, and §Related Work on Amoeba) requires `recommendation: "review"` and `recommendation: "blocked"` as a stable vocabulary that runners route on. TD-7 instead shows free-text recommendations (`'Review required before advancing'`, `'Blocked: review verdict does not clear threshold'`) and says "Exact strings finalized in implementation." But line 286 promises "`review` / `blocked` recommendation vocabulary — the stable strings runners route on." The two cannot both hold, and leaving it to implementation means 242, 243 and Amoeba have no fixed contract. Existing recommendations are human-readable text, which is probably why the design drifted. Fix: pick one. Either emit the literal tokens `review`/`blocked` as named constants (human text goes in `summary`/`rationale`), or record a deliberate deviation from the arch and name the exact stable strings in this document.

findings.title: A runner has to parse the rationale to learn which review to run
findings.description: `pending-review` and `review-failed` now cover four boundaries (`arch`/`slice`/`tasks`/`code`). The review type appears only in `rationale` (line 268). The `NextAction` shape is frozen and `SliceStatus` has no review-type field. So a runner that has to choose an arch, slice, tasks or code review agent must parse free text. That breaks the arch's design goal that "runners can act on them without parsing recommendation strings," and the slice's own value statement (line 41). Fix: carry the review type somewhere machine-readable within the existing shape. Options are the existing optional `phase` field, or a recommendation token per review type. Then add a test that asserts it for each boundary.

findings.title: The pre-slice-plan (`arch`) boundary is under-specified
findings.description:
The slice plan assigns the `arch` boundary to 241, but the design only says "extend the no-active-slice / pre-slice-plan path." Three gaps follow:
- **Index:** `detectDocuments` takes a slice index, and with no active slice `deriveSliceStatus` has no index. The design never says which index the `NNN-review.arch.*.md` lookup uses. Presumably it is the arch index derived from `fileArch`.
- **Status:** with no active slice there is no `SliceStatus` to set to `pending-review`/`review-failed`, so TD-3's claim that "status flows through `getStatus()`" does not hold here.
- **Routing:** the reserved `LIFECYCLE: review-gate` branch is in the active-slice path, so it never handles this case. The no-active-slice guard also has more than one place that recommends creating the slice plan, including the first-run guidance ("Architecture document exists. Advance to Phase 3…"). Each of those needs the gate, or the gate can be bypassed.

Fix: state the index source, how the gated state is represented when there is no active slice, and every recommendation site the gate must wrap. Add a test for each of those sites.

findings.title: Gates are not cumulative: creating the next artifact skips the gate
findings.description: Each gate fires only while CF is sitting at that boundary. If a user creates the task file without a `slice` review, the slice moves to pre-implementation and the `slice` review is never checked again. The same happens if all task boxes get checked between two `cf next` calls: the `tasks` review is skipped and only `code` is required. This sits uneasily with the design's central claim that "every phase boundary owes exactly one review" (line 19). The 242 consistency rule as specified only covers completed slices, so it would not catch these skips. Fix: state explicitly whether earlier-boundary reviews stay required. Either make the gate check all prior boundaries up to the current position, or keep current-boundary-only and say why the skip is acceptable. Also reconcile the two definitions of the pre-implementation trigger: "not implemented" (line 25) and "not complete" (line 138).

findings.title: Arch requirement to name parse failures in the rationale is dropped
findings.description: The arch (§Technical Considerations, "File-read failure modes") says: "The rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." The design deliberately collapses read failures and missing frontmatter into "no `verdict`" (line 79). TD-7's rationale requirements (line 268) list review type, verdict and threshold, but not parse failure. Under the default policy, `review_unknown_as = fail`, an unreadable file therefore looks the same as a `verdict: FAIL` file, with no observable signal. That is a silent failure under the project's failure-mode rule. `parseFrontmatter` already returns `found: false` when the file can't be read or parsed, which is enough to tell "unreadable" apart from "present, no verdict." Fix: carry that distinction through `reviewGate`, name it in the `review-failed` rationale (or `warnings`), and add a test that asserts the signal for an unparseable fixture.

findings.title: `resolveGateConfig` contract is inconsistent and can't resolve per-boundary thresholds
findings.description:
The design contradicts itself in four places:
- **Who reads config:** line 109 says the navigator calls `this.config?.get(...)` and hands raw values to `reviewGate`, while lines 56 and 191 have `resolveGateConfig(config)` read `ConfigManager` itself.
- **Missing parameter:** the signature takes no `Boundary`, yet TD-4 requires it to return the per-boundary threshold override.
- **Key mapping:** `Boundary` values are camelCase (`preAdvance`), but the shipped config keys are `workflow.review_gates.pre_advance.threshold`. The boundary-to-key mapping is not defined, which leaves room for the scattered magic strings the design itself forbids (line 276).
- **Hedging:** lines 56, 154, 191 and 309 still say "if retained," although TD-4 decides to retain and consume the override.

Fix: choose one owner for config reads, give `resolveGateConfig` a `boundary` parameter, add the config-key segment to the `BOUNDARY_REVIEW_TYPE`-style single source of truth, and remove the hedges.

findings.title: No fail-fast behavior for invalid config values read at evaluation time
findings.description: The arch principle "Fail-fast on configuration errors" says an invalid value must not cause a silent pass or a silent block. Enum validation only applies at `cf config set`. A hand-edited `.context-forge.toml` with `review_enabled = "true"` (a string) fails the planned `=== true` check, so gating turns off silently. A bogus `review_threshold` token has no defined handling in `evaluateVerdict`. The design should say that out-of-type or out-of-enum values found at read time raise a config error, and that this error propagates out of status derivation instead of being absorbed into a default status. Add a test for each case.

findings.title: UNKNOWN is never `pending`, which differs slightly from the arch wording
findings.description: The arch allows `pending-review` "if verdict is UNKNOWN and `review_unknown_as` treats it as pending." The `review_unknown_as` enum shipped in 240 has no pending value, so the slice's rule (a present artifact is never `pending`) is consistent with the shipped config. It is also the safer reading. 243 should document it.

findings.title: Layering, dependency direction and conservative default
findings.description:
These all match the arch:
- `reviewGate.ts` is pure and has no dependency on the navigator, so 242 can import it without pulling in the navigator.
- `ConfigManager` comes in through an optional constructor argument, which keeps config file I/O out of the core logic and inherits the worktree-scoped resolution from initiative 180.
- With gating off, behavior is unchanged structurally, and a regression test enforces it.
- The `code` trigger, checkbox completion (TD-5), keeps CF artifact-shaped.
- The decision matrix (TD-2) matches the arch's verdict rules, including how `unknownAs=concerns` interacts with the threshold.

findings.title: Scope is in line with the slice plan
findings.description: All four boundaries, the two statuses, the evaluator, the injection and the `STATUS` const are all assigned to 241 by the slice plan, and all are present. Deferrals to 242, 243 and 910 match the plan. Nothing beyond the plan is added, and the size of the design fits a 4/5-effort slice.

structured_findings.summary: Recommendation vocabulary contradicts the arch and the slice's own integration contract
A runner has to parse the rationale to learn which review to run
Gates are not cumulative: creating the next artifact skips the gate
Arch requirement to name parse failures in the rationale is dropped
`resolveGateConfig` contract is inconsistent and can't resolve per-boundary thresholds
No fail-fast behavior for invalid config values read at evaluation time
UNKNOWN is never `pending`, which differs slightly from the arch wording
Layering, dependency direction and conservative default
Scope is in line with the slice plan
